title: Democrat Eileen Laubacher Upsets Lauren Boebert in Shocking Colorado House Race
snippet: In a major political upset, retired Navy Rear Adm. Eileen Laubacher has defeated incumbent Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's conservative 4th Congressional District.
content:
In one of the most stunning political upsets of the midterm election cycle, incumbent Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert has lost her seat in Colorado's 4th Congressional District to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher.

The Associated Press officially called the race on Friday afternoon. With 99% of the votes counted, Laubacher secured 48.8% of the vote (187,488 votes), while Boebert trailed close behind at 47.9% (184,047 votes). Libertarian candidate Douglas Mangeris captured 3.3% of the vote.

A Seismic Shift in a Conservative Stronghold

The defeat marks a remarkable turn of events in a district long considered the most heavily Republican area in Colorado. Laubacher's win adds Colorado's 4th District to a growing tally of more than 40 Republican-held seats that have flipped to Democrats nationwide during these midterms.

Boebert, an ardent defender of gun rights and one of former President Donald Trump's most visible allies on Capitol Hill, had previously represented Colorado's 3rd Congressional District. After barely surviving a reelection bid there in 2022 by just 546 votes, she relocated to the much redder 4th District in late 2023 to secure a safer electoral path.

Addressing the race on Thursday, Boebert pointed to broader national headwinds for her party, citing gas prices, foreign conflicts, and unaddressed corruption in Washington. She also argued that members of the right-wing House Freedom Caucus were ignored when urging leadership to address core voter concerns like government surveillance and election integrity.

Who Is Eileen Laubacher?

Laubacher, a newcomer to elected office, brings a decades-long career in military intelligence to Congress. She served 34 years in the U.S. Navy before retiring in 2024 as a rear admiral, following in the footsteps of a family tradition of naval service. Her career included a deployment to Afghanistan in 2009, a senior diplomatic posting in India, and a position on the National Security Council during the Biden administration.

A lifelong Republican for much of her adulthood, Laubacher formally registered as a Democrat in late 2025, stating that the GOP had become "nearly unrecognizable" to her. Despite a legal challenge from a primary opponent over her recent party registration, she prevailed on the primary ballot and ran a campaign tailored to moderates.

Her platform emphasized fiscal responsibility, support for middle-class tax cuts, strong immigration enforcement, and addressing living costs by rolling back tariffs.

The End of a Tumultuous Tenure

Boebert's departure from the House closes out a high-profile, highly contentious period in Washington. First elected in 2020, she gained national attention as an outspoken critic of federal authority and a promoter of claims surrounding the 2020 election results.

During her tenure, she introduced resolutions to impeach top administration officials and played a prominent role in the high-stakes 2023 House speaker battle that lasted 15 rounds of voting. Outside of policy debates, her personal conduct also drew headline coverage, notably following a September 2023 incident where she was removed from a Denver theater production for disruptive behavior.

While her move to the 4th District paid dividends in her previous campaign, it was not enough to insulate the congresswoman from a nationwide surge in Democratic turnout that reshaped the delegation in Colorado and beyond.
